newsitem.title: USA: Ashland confirms unit sale likely soon.
newsitem.headline: Ashland confirms unit sale likely soon.

text.p: The chief executive of Ashland Inc said the company is in talks to sell its exploration unit rather than pursue an initial public offering.
"We have taken bids. We are evaluating those bids. We are currently in negotiations with the people who appear most likely," Paul Chellgren told Reuters in a telephone interview.
He also characterized a sale of the unit as "highly likely" and said a transaction would likely take place soon.
Reuters earlier reported that Ashland was close to selling the exploration unit for about $600 million.

Chellgren did not identify potential buyers, but sources familiar with the talks identified them as Equitable Resources Inc and privately-held Eastern Group, which is 83 percent-owned by Norway's Statoil.
Chellgren also confirmed that recent interest in Appalachian properties contributed to the company's decision to sell the unit rather than spin it off.
